chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū ʿAlī Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, who said: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥārith al-Qazwīnī narrated to me, saying:

I was with my father in Surrā man Raʾā, and my father used to practice veterinary work in the stable of Abū Muḥammad. He said: Al-Mustaʿīn had a mule the like of which had not been seen in beauty and size, and it would refuse its back, the bridle, and the saddle. Trainers had been gathered against it, but it gave them no means to ride it.

He said: One of his close companions said to him, "O Commander of the Faithful, why do you not send for al-Ḥasan ibn al-Riḍā so that he may come? Either he will ride it, or it will kill him, and you will be relieved of him."

He said: So he sent for Abū Muḥammad, and my father went with him. My father said: When Abū Muḥammad entered the residence, I was with him. Abū Muḥammad looked at the mule standing in the courtyard of the house, then turned toward it and placed his hand on its croup. He said: I looked at the mule, and it had sweated until perspiration flowed from it. Then he went to al-Mustaʿīn and greeted him. He welcomed him and brought him near, then said, "O Abū Muḥammad, bridle this mule." So Abū Muḥammad said to my father, "Bridle it, O boy." Al-Mustaʿīn said, "You bridle it." So he put down his cloak, then stood and bridled it, then returned to his seat and sat down.

Then he said to him, "O Abū Muḥammad, saddle it." So he said to my father, "O boy, saddle it." He said, "You saddle it." So he stood a second time and saddled it, then returned. Then he said to him, "Do you think you can ride it?" He said, "Yes." So he rode it without it resisting him. Then he galloped it in the residence, then set it to a graceful gait, and it walked in the finest manner possible. Then he returned and dismounted.

Then al-Mustaʿīn said to him, "O Abū Muḥammad, how did you find it?" He said, "O Commander of the Faithful, I have not seen its like in beauty and vigor, and it is only fitting that the like of it should belong to the Commander of the Faithful." He said: Then he said, "O Abū Muḥammad, the Commander of the Faithful has bestowed it upon you." So Abū Muḥammad said to my father, "O boy, take it." So my father took it and led it away.

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: the kunyah of Imam al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام in this report
key_terms.السَّرْجَ: the saddle placed on the animal for riding
key_terms.اللِّجَامَ: the bridle placed on the animal
key_terms.الْبَيْطَرَةَ: veterinary practice or treatment of animals
key_terms.الْمُسْتَعِينِ: Al-Mustaʿīn, the Abbasid ruler mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْهَمْلَجَةِ: a graceful, brisk, elegant gait in riding
key_terms.بَغْلٌ: a mule central to the event of the narration

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe a sign of Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام through the taming of al-Mustaʿīn’s mule?
ai.summary: This report narrates an episode in which Abū Muḥammad عليه السلام was summoned before al-Mustaʿīn to deal with an exceptionally difficult mule that no one could control. By the Imam’s presence and action, the animal became subdued, and he then bridled, saddled, and rode it with ease, after which it was gifted to him. The narration highlights a sign of the Imam’s distinction and the political atmosphere surrounding him.
